Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown or black circular lesions on leaf surfaces, premature defoliation, and scabby lesions on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungal pathogen Venturia inaequalis overwintering in fallen leaves and spreading via splashing spring rains.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune dense branches to enhance sunlight penetration and airflow. Apply protective sprays before rainy periods.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_treatment: Spray sulfur or liquid copper formulations at bud break. Apply neem oil spray or potassium bicarbonate during early symptom onset.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Captan 50WP, Mancozeb, or Myclobutanil fungicidal spray according to local agricultural extension schedules.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots enlarging into concentric rings with tan centers (frogeye appearance). Can cause limb cankers and black mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa entering through wounds, dead tissue, or insect punctures.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out diseased wood and dead twigs at least 15 cm below cankers. Remove mummified fruit remaining on the tree.
Apple___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Copper-based fungicides applied at green tip stage. Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis.
Apple___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Thiophanate-methyl, Captan, or Fludioxonil applications during the growing season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish spots on upper leaf surfaces. Later produces tube-like fungal structures on undersides of leaves.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Heteroecious rust fungus requiring both juniper/cedar trees and apple trees to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Avoid planting susceptible apple trees near Eastern Red Cedar. Remove cedar galls before spore dispersal in early spring.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_treatment: Sulfur sprays starting when pink blossom buds emerge until petal fall. Bordeaux mixture.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil or Chlorothalonil applied at 7-10 day intervals from blossom cluster through cover sprays.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Foliage exhibits vigorous green coloration, uniform leaf texture, clear veins, and no necrotic lesions or discoloration.
Apple___healthy.cause: N/A — Optimal plant nutrition, appropriate sunlight, and effective disease management.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain standard orchard hygiene, balanced N-P-K fertilization, timely pruning, and routine canopy inspections.
Apple___healthy.organic_treatment: Foliar application of seaweed extract, compost tea, or micronutrient foliar spray to bolster natural plant defense.
Apple___healthy.chemical_treatment: No fungicide required. Maintain balanced micronutrients (Zinc, Boron, Calcium) during vegetative growth.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Oval to elongate reddish-brown cinnamon pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture the epidermis to release powdery spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Airborne spores of Puccinia sorghi carried by wind currents during cool, humid weather (16-24°C).
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant or tolerant corn hybrids. Practice crop rotation and maintain balanced nitrogen levels without over-fertilizing.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_treatment: Neem seed extract spray and copper sulfate foliar sprays during early vegetative phases.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_treatment: Azoxystrobin, Pyraclostrobin, or Propiconazole foliar fungicides when pustules appear before tassel emergence.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) developing parallel to leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungus overwintering in corn crop debris, favored by extended dew and moderate temperatures.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Deep tillage to bury infected residues, 1-2 year crop rotation with non-host crops, and planting certified resistant varieties.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_treatment: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens microbial inoculants and certified copper hydroxide solutions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.chemical_treatment: Trifloxystrobin + Prothioconazole or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole applied at early infection stages.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant dark green leaves with strong midribs, uniform cellular expansion, and no fungal lesions or chlorosis.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.cause: N/A — Adequate soil moisture, balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium availability.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain optimal plant spacing for ventilation, weed control, and integrated soil nutrient management.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.organic_treatment: Periodic compost tea applications or vermicompost top-dressing to sustain beneficial rhizosphere microorganisms.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.chemical_treatment: No fungicide required. Apply balanced NPK fertilizers (e.g. 10-10-10 or 20-20-20) in split applications.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small, circular reddish-brown spots with dark borders on leaves. Tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) form inside spots.
Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungal infection thriving in warm (21-27°C), wet conditions during spring shoot growth.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out mummified berry clusters and infected canes during dormancy. Keep vineyard floor clear of diseased litter.
Grape___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Liquid copper sprays or lime sulfur during pre-bloom to post-bloom intervals.
Grape___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb, Ziram, or Kresoxim-methyl applied from 2-inch shoot stage until 4 weeks after bloom.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dark brown, angular to irregular necrotic spots on foliage, often coalescing to cause extensive scorching and leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungal pathogen favored by warm, humid microclimates within dense vine canopies.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Shoot thinning and leaf pulling around fruit zones to facilitate rapid drying of foliage after rainfall.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.organic_treatment: Neem oil emulsions, potassium bicarbonate, and copper-based foliar protectants.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.chemical_treatment: Carbendazim, Chlorothalonil, or Boscalid sprayed at initial symptom appearance.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant emerald green leaves with intact palmate lobes, clear vein architecture, and zero fungal spots.
Grape___healthy.cause: N/A — Excellent canopy management, good airflow, and balanced vineyard irrigation.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper trellis wire training, routine canopy management, and regular soil testing.
Grape___healthy.organic_treatment: Seaweed liquid extract and foliar potassium spray during veraison to promote berry sweetness.
Grape___healthy.chemical_treatment: No fungicide required. Standard foliar micronutrient applications (Magnesium, Zinc) as needed.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown to black spots with concentric rings resembling a target board or bullseye, typically starting on older bottom leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus Alternaria solani surviving in solanaceous plant residue and favored by fluctuating wet/dry weather.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops with non-solanaceous species for at least 3 years. Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Copper octanoate spray, Bacillus subtilis bio-pesticide, and bio-friendly compost extracts.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole applied at early flowering and repeated every 7-10 days.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark brown to purplish-black water-soaked lesions on leaf tips or irregular sunken brown dry rot patches on tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans — notorious organism responsible for the Irish potato famine.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers. Destroy cull piles. Scout fields diligently in cool, foggy weather.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Fixed copper fungicides (copper sulfate / copper hydroxide) applied preventatively before rain events.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold), Cymoxanil, or Dimethomorph applied preventatively.

Potato___Common_scab.symptoms: Corky, rough, brown raised or pitted scabby surface lesions on potato tuber skin. Lesions reduce marketability and quality.
Potato___Common_scab.cause: Soil-dwelling bacterium/actinomycete Streptomyces scabies favored by dry, warm soils with pH > 5.5.
Potato___Common_scab.prevention: Maintain soil pH between 5.0 and 5.2. Maintain uniform soil moisture during tuber initiation (2 to 6 weeks post-emergence). Avoid excessive liming.
Potato___Common_scab.organic_treatment: Apply elemental agricultural sulfur to acidify soil. Use beneficial Trichoderma or Bacillus microbial bio-fungicides.
Potato___Common_scab.chemical_treatment: Seed tuber fungicide treatment (Fludioxonil or Mancozeb) prior to planting.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, uniform, clean skin without lesions or corky blemishes; or rich green composite foliage free of blight lesions.
Potato___healthy.cause: N/A — Optimal soil conditions, proper irrigation, balanced nutrition.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper soil fertility, crop rotation, and routine field scouting.
Potato___healthy.organic_treatment: Balanced organic compost, kelp extract, and regular hilling.
Potato___healthy.chemical_treatment: No treatment required. Maintain standard micronutrient balance.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy water-soaked spots (1-3 mm) on leaves, often surrounded by a distinctive yellow halo. Leaves turn brown and drop.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial pathogen entering through natural stomata openings and insect or storm-induced leaf wounds.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds and transplants. Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet. Sterilize stakes and tools.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Copper-based bactericides paired with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biological controls.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb (to overcome copper resistance in bacterial strains).

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with characteristic concentric rings (target board pattern) beginning on lowest, oldest leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal pathogen residing in infected tomato plant debris and warm, rainy conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch around plants to prevent soil splashing onto bottom leaves. Prune lower 12 inches of foliage as plants mature.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Copper soap spray, neem oil extract, and baking soda solution (1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp horticultural oil per gallon).
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin, or Mancozeb applied every 7-14 days as preventative protectant.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, pale green to brown water-soaked blotches that expand rapidly. White downy sporulation on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans spores spread over long distances by wind during cool, wet, foggy conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant). Ensure spacious plant spacing. Destroy volunteer tomato plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) applied thoroughly before rainfall cycles.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Mandipropamid (Revus), Metalaxyl + Mancozeb, or Fluopicolide applied as preventative spray.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow chlorotic spots on upper leaf surfaces. Undersides develop olive-green to brownish velvety fungal patches.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal spores flourishing in environments with high relative humidity (>85%) and moderate temperatures (21-24°C), common in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Provide adequate greenhouse ventilation and spacing. Avoid overhead watering to keep leaf surfaces dry.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic_treatment: Potassium bicarbonate spray (MilStop) and bio-fungicides containing Streptomyces lydicus.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with gray or tan centers and sharp dark brown margins. Tiny black specks visible inside center.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus overwintering in plant debris and solanaceous weeds (such as nightshade), dispersed by splashing water.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Implement a 3-year crop rotation. Apply organic mulch layer (straw or wood chips). Prune infected bottom leaves early.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_treatment: Copper octanoate sprays and regular sulfur dusting at the first sign of leaf spotting.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Pyraclostrobin applied at 7-10 day intervals during wet periods.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Marked upward cupping and curling of leaf margins, severe stunting of shoots, chlorotic leaf yellowing, and flower drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Begomovirus transmitted exclusively by the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Install fine mesh screens in greenhouses. Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids. Use yellow sticky traps to monitor whitefly vectors.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_treatment: Insecticidal soap, horticultural mineral oil, and pyrethrin sprays to eliminate the whitefly insect vectors. Remove infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_treatment: Target whitefly vectors with Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran, or Spiromesifen. No direct chemical cure exists for the virus once infected.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep emerald compound foliage with serrated leaflet margins, crisp aromatic scent, robust turgor, and clear leaf tissue.
Tomato___healthy.cause: N/A — Excellent nutrition, optimal sunlight (6-8 hours), well-drained loamy soil, and proper staking.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain consistent deep root watering, bottom leaf pruning, and periodic companion planting with basil and marigolds.
Tomato___healthy.organic_treatment: Liquid fish emulsion, seaweed extract, and calcium nitrate foliar spray to prevent blossom end rot.
Tomato___healthy.chemical_treatment: No fungicide required. Apply high-potassium soluble tomato food (e.g., 5-10-10 or 4-18-38) once fruit set begins.
